newsitem.title: USA: Ill. bill to disclose bond buyers names unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Ill. bill to disclose bond buyers names unlikely.

text.p: An Illinois lawmaker who sponsored a bill requiring disclosure of the names and addresses of anyone who buys any state debt said Thursday it is "highly unlikely" the provision would move forward this year.
Rep. Jeff Schoenberg, D-Evanston, said that the provision requiring the disclosure was excised from pending legislation several weeks ago and very unlikely to be revived again this session.
The bill would have required the state comptroller to compile and maintain a list of names and addresses of all persons and entities that buy any type of state debt.
The list would have been available for public review upon request or over the Internet.
The bill itself remains pending for possible "framework" for any settlement of outstanding issues involving certificates of participation reforms, Schoenberg said.

Schoenberg is one of a group of House Democrats who filed a lawsuit last year challenging the legality of $19.2 million of insured COPs sold for a state public aid department building in downtown Chicago.
That lawsuit remains pending in Cook County Circuit Court.
